epic.title: WPP at Scale
epic.overview: Take the operational learnings from the first WPP pilot market and build them into the platform so the remaining WPP markets are easier to run than the first, with each feature designed to serve more than just WPP where possible.

milestones.title: M1 — Core Operational Efficiency
milestones.overview: The foundational bulk-management and monitoring tools research leads need to run large WPP projects day to day: survey compatibility, bulk survey actions, external panels, targeting bucket filtering, automated field reporting and WPP dashboard.

milestones.title: M2 — Expansion & Follow-On Builds
milestones.overview: Real-Time Survey Translation and Quota Management Between Cells require further conversation before build. Externalise Hardcoded Script Values is ready to build but was grouped here to keep M1 focused.

milestones.title: M3 — WPP API Platform
milestones.overview: Stand up fieldwork-api — a new, separately hosted serverless API (AWS Lambda/TypeScript, own repo) that (a) provides the data layer for the WPP Dashboard (F1.6) and (b) takes ownership of everything currently served by src/routes/wpp in dashboard-api (/wpp, /wpp/exports, /wppMonitoring), restructured for the ~470-cell multi-market scale of 2026-W1.

milestones.title: M4- WPP Dashboard
milestones.overview: Provide WPP with a dashboard showing how markets are progressing — a single up-to-date view of market progress without manual reporting. The dashboard is a static web app reading the hourly per-market MetricsSnapshot JSON from S3 (produced by M3 / F3.3); it does not read the database directly and has no backend of its own.

features.title: F1.1 — Excel Template & Survey Compatibility
features.overview: Validate the survey template against the demographic questions in the questions Excel before survey creation, to ensure the survey structure will be compatible with downstream coding and data delivery processes. Only demographic questions are validated at this stage, since other questions and options may be populated after creation (e.g., assigned to users later). This prevents launching surveys with mismatched demographic questions, options, or response values that could lead to incorrect data processing later.
features.rationale: Signed off; the validation-gate PRs cover all three ACs end to end, though 3 of the 5 stories are JIRA-Done without a master-confirmed PR.

features.title: F2.1 — Real-Time Survey Translation
features.overview: One survey per project, scripted once by the research team, holding all of the languages required. Respondents are shown their local language, while the responses are automatically mapped back to English at the point of capture, so there is no need to build or maintain separate English/French/Arabic versions of the same survey.

features.title: F3.1 — Platform Foundation (fieldwork-api)
features.overview: Stand up the wpp-api repo and its platform layer so business-logic migration can begin: SAM/CircleCI scaffold with lint-enforced layer boundaries, shared config/logging/error handling, Firebase JWT auth with wpp:user/wpp:admin scopes, the full test harness (Firebase emulators + LocalStack + OpenAPI docs), all repository interfaces, and the Firestore-backed cell registry that replaces the hardcoded SURVEY_CELLS/BRAND_NAME constants.
features.rationale: Signed off and its one tracked story (a Playwright pipeline-to-dashboard E2E test) is shipped, but the feature's other stated ACs — CI lint/layer-boundary enforcement, JWT-auth rejection, and the cell-registry endpoint — have no PR evidence under this feature's own tracked work.

acCoverage.label: CI enforces build/lint/tests and layer-boundary import rules
A request without a valid Firebase JWT or scope is rejected
The cell registry serves seeded data and its refresh endpoint requires admin scope
The integration suite exercises repositories against emulators/LocalStack, including redelivery idempotency

features.title: F3.2 — Endpoint Migration: QC, Exports, Monitoring (fieldwork-processing)
features.overview: Move all existing WPP business logic out of dashboard-api into fieldwork-processingi with payload/file parity: the Quality Control engine (runner + ~18 methods, bucket adjust, backfill, soft-remove), the 7 file exports, and all monitoring endpoints — with one deliberate behaviour change: every file-producing endpoint becomes an async job (trigger → status → presigned download) backed by SQS + S3, replacing the Redis job store.
features.rationale: Product signed this off as Done and JIRA marks the single tracked story Done, but zero PRs are linked to this feature — nothing here confirms any of the endpoint-migration work described actually shipped.

acCoverage.label: Old and new endpoints produce identical output against the same seed data
Worker crashes or SQS redelivery never produce duplicate artifacts or state transitions
A non-admin token calling an admin-only route gets a 403
Downloads re-check authorization and stream via presigned URL rather than local disk or buffering

features.title: F3.3 — Dashboard Metrics
features.overview:
Deliver the data layer for the WPP fieldwork dashboard (F1.6): an hourly per-market metrics snapshot produced inside the fieldwork-processing Step Functions workflow (EventBridge hourly start → discover → fail-closed QC gate → per-market metrics compute → S3). Each successful cycle writes a validated, aggregate-only MetricsSnapshot JSON to a dedicated snapshot bucket:

There is no HTTP API in v1 (design change 2026-08-05): the previously planned /v1/dashboard/* endpoints, ?fresh=true recompute, OpenAPI client codegen, and per-market SQS fan-out are all gone. The dashboard reads the snapshot JSON directly from S3; the embedded computedAt is the UI's "last sync" indicator. There is no per-request recompute path.

v1 is scoped to data we already capture: completes vs target, starts/in-progress/IR%, screen-out breakdown, per-QC-check counts, research-defender counts, quota-cell fill, LOI (average/median/per-section), daily completes, grade/region tallies, and per-cell drill-down data. Derived values (percentages, deltas, totals) are deliberately not stored — consumers compute them. Forecast/RAG/Fount go-live metrics are v2, blocked on WPP supplying field dates.
features.rationale: Product signed this off as Done, but scoreBasis shows 5 todo and 2 in-progress subtasks still outstanding out of 28 — the metrics/QC/snapshot core is built and well-evidenced across the fieldwork-processing PR chain, while several export-layer product decisions (WPP consideration-answer handling, custom-boolean labels, anonymous-respondent display) remain open.

acCoverage.label: The dashboard polls a per-market snapshot with no viewer fanning out to Firestore
A failed market compute preserves the last-known-good snapshot and badges it stale
A delayed or duplicate write can never overwrite a newer snapshot
The snapshot validates against a strict, versioned schema with aggregates only, no PII
A QC failure anywhere fails the cycle closed, leaving the existing snapshot untouched

features.title: F4.1 — Dashboard
features.overview: Build the static WPP fieldwork dashboard app: a rebuild matching the WPP BAV “Fieldwork Command Centre” prototype design (share link — a design guide, not a contract; we do not reuse its source), consuming the per-market MetricsSnapshot JSON produced by fieldwork-processing (F3.3 / BOUN-11442). No backend: the page reads S3-served JSON only.
features.rationale: Signed off; JIRA marks this Done but hasn't been confirmed reaching master. The one PR ships the core dashboard (market switching, quota meters, daily completes charts), but its body doesn't speak to the UI-polish, client-side-derivation, demo-QC labelling, or test-coverage ACs.

acCoverage.label: A separate, static app is typed against the snapshot schema
The UI is clean and minimal with bold labels
The dashboard polls the snapshot on an interval with no direct Firestore access or per-request recompute
The market overview renders the full set of v1 content blocks
Derived values are computed client-side rather than stored in the snapshot
The dashboard works against demo-QC snapshots so UI work doesn't wait on the QC port
Derived-value computations and components have fixture-driven tests

features.title: F4.4 — Staleness badging & data-status UX
features.overview: Make data trustworthiness visible: users should always know how fresh the numbers are, when they're degraded, and which panels aren't real yet. This is the UI half of the pipeline's staleness contract (markStale in MetricsSnapshotS3Store).
features.rationale: Product signed this off as Done and JIRA marks the single story Done, but zero PRs are linked to this feature — none of the staleness-badging, fetch-failure, or demo-QC-labelling behaviour in its ACs has any PR evidence.

acCoverage.label: A visible last-sync timestamp renders on every view
A stale-flagged snapshot shows a degraded-data banner while keeping last-known-good metrics
An unflagged but old snapshot shows the same degraded banner client-side
Date-derived v2 panels stay hidden rather than zero-filled until field dates exist
Demo-QC panels carry a clear marker while QC data mode is demo
A failed poll keeps the last rendered data with a connection-lost indicator
Each state (fresh, stale, silently-stale, demo-QC, fetch-failed) has component tests
